server_cross_reference.interpretation: The original EI server configuration gives an exact map-stem to FMMap/MMap frame cross-reference for this distribution. It explains why the client-side map object has two libraries; it is not a substitute for the executable's rendering path.

mmap.common_offsets: Most observed frames carry WIL offsetX=-24, offsetY=-16; the small frames 35–38 use offsetX=7, offsetY=-44.
mmap.interpretation: MMap is a multi-resolution map image family; the selected frame is later clipped/scaled into the 128×128 destination rather than being a 128×128 source itself.

fmmap.common_offsets: Frames 0–28 generally carry WIL offsetX=-24, offsetY=-16; Frame 30 is offsetX=0, offsetY=0.
fmmap.interpretation: FMMap is the full-map/large-map resource family; the original server cross-reference maps overland/city entries to its frames. Its dimensions are materially larger than the fixed minimap destination and must be displayed through a scroll/zoom viewport.

selection.frame_expression: map_id - 1000 for FMMap; map_id for MMap
selection.warning: The selected frame proves the resource/index relation, not yet the visible UI widget or final screen destination.

map_id_update_trace.destination_reset: The selected frame width/height are written into owner+0x2E0 and the current view position is passed to 0x0043D5F0.

static_initializer_trace.interpretation: The executable initializes both map libraries and a 128×128 surface before any map ID is selected. This is stronger than inferring the map source from a screenshot: the two library fields and the branch-specific frame-header path are statically explicit.

viewport.surface_size_basis: The constructor at 0x0043D4D0 calls 0x0043D5F0 with width=128 and height=128; 0x0043DE40 later rebuilds the same surface as 256×256 or 128×128.

fixed_minimap_widget.basis: The initializer pushes bottom=0x80, right=0x320, top=0 and left=0x2A0 before the SetRect IAT call for owner+0x2C0.
fixed_minimap_widget.interpretation: This is the original fixed 800x600 minimap destination at the top-right edge. The constructor passes a 128×128 map surface; the display-mode routine can rebuild it as 256×256.

viewport.notes: The map subsystem maintains a source/view rectangle and selects a 4096 or 6144 surface mode based on loaded map metadata. The destination widget rectangle is now statically recovered as 128x128 at screen (672,0).

mode_switch.behavior: On a successful toggle, the routine negates owner+0x294 and rebuilds the map surface through 0x0043D5F0.

keyboard_dispatch_evidence.caveat: The numeric key code is exact; the user-facing label and whether this is called full-map/minimap are not named in the binary.

adjacent_key_evidence.behavior: The same input reader tests key 0x59 and toggles main+0x64A4 when the map/world guard is active; no direct map-surface rebuild occurs in this branch.
